context: Request: all Capital Markets matters with a Rule 144A or Regulation S tranche, with offering documents and deal records showing structure and closing. Rubric: seven matters (1005-00002, 1014-00001, 1016-00003, 1021-00002, 1039-00002, 1045-00001 closed; 1020-00003 executed-but-terminated precedent) with named proof documents (e.g. 1021-00002 closing-index-and-signature-pages.docx), plus a precision criterion (1024-00004 Driftwood CLO and unclosed deals are outside the set).

stages.note: Two parallel batches of opening reads of offering memoranda, notes, purchase agreements and closing memos of the seven matters it shortlisted; reviewer said partly (status records of unclosed candidates not yet read).

stages.note: declared: Read a chosen matter's documents in depth (attempt 2); reads status, termination and closing memos of suspended, terminated and sibling candidates; several guessed paths do not exist.

stages.note: Lists the files of ten sibling candidate matters and one more; reviewer said partly (guessed paths, sibling dismissals from listings).

stages.stage: Check or revise the response
stages.note: Re-reads the response and checks that cited paths exist; reviewer said partly (only path existence checked).

stages.stage: Finish the run
stages.note: Calls finish.

divergence: All three runs failed. They shared the procedure: store listing, folder listing, store-wide extraction scans (with timeouts and reruns), then batches of opening reads across the shortlisted matters, one write and a path check. All three counted a structured-credit matter as qualifying at the write stage (over-inclusion). T0 differed in excluding an executed-then-terminated deal it had read (first error at the write stage). T1 and T2 failed first at their first screening reads, which skipped a closing index they had listed, and then bucketed one or two closed deals as not closed and added unclosed matters. Reviews at every stage repeated the same generic flags (unopened surfaced matters, possible under-inclusion); the write review's over-inclusion flag in T1 led to two revision passes that left the extra matters in place.
